symptom: Every QUAL004 finding (and CONV001-010, the SEC rules, most bundled Starlark rules, and missing_translations) prints its location with the module twice: `at M.M.NAV_Home`, `at Sales.Sales.Order.Status`; CONV018's module-level finding prints `at Sales.Sales`
cause: `Location.DocumentName` is documented as the document's own name and `QualifiedName()` prefixes the module, but ~30 bundled Starlark rules pass `document_name=<x>.qualified_name`, as does the Go rule missing_translations. CONV018 passes the module as the document of a module-level finding
insight: Fix the one place the name is assembled, not the rules: text, Markdown, SARIF and `lint -d` all go through `QualifiedName()`, and fixing ~30 rule files would leave every project's stale `mxcli init` copies and every user-written rule still doubling. It is safe to strip on prefix because a Mendix document name cannot contain a dot, so a leading `<module>.` is always the module; the controls are a document named like its module (`Sales.Sales` stays) and a module name that is a prefix of the document's (`M` + `MX_Home`). The JSON `document` field still carries whichever spelling the rule passed — `lint -d` already accepts both. Found while reproducing ako/mxcli#1484
